result:
I fixed one problem: two new pilot runs were sharing cores with a running one. Everything else is healthy and both queues are empty.

**Running:** 9 FEBio pilot runs, 5 pilotCS (p061, p083, p120, p129, p062) and 4 pilotCR9 (p061, p083, p129, p062). Every log is 1–6 s old and every run moved forward since 14:27 (+0.03 to +0.55 in t). The two p062 jobs were launched at 14:29–14:30, just after the last report. No job finished in the last hour.

**The fix:**
- **Problem:** the 14:29 p062 launches were given cores 28–32 while pilotCS_p129 was still running on 28–31. pilotCR9_p062 had all 4 threads on one CPU (cpu32); pilotCS_p062 had 4 threads on 3 CPUs. This is the known scheduler gap: it protects only runs younger than 300 s, and an older GPU run can look idle in its 3-second load sample.
- **What I did:** moved both runs onto idle cores in NUMA node 2, where their memory is. pilotCR9_p062 went to cores 36–39 and pilotCS_p062 to 32–35. I re-pinned each FEBio process and its h31 parent, so later split windows keep the new cores. The cores and their hyper-thread partners were 100 % idle first. No core is shared now.
- **Result:**
  - pilotCR9_p062 went from 179 % to 306 % CPU.
  - pilotCS_p062 stayed about the same (276 % → 271 %), now on 4 separate CPUs.
  - The account total went from 26.97 to 28.80 of 32 cores.

**Resources:**
- **CPU** is the limit: 36 FEBio threads on a 32-core quota. 20 % of CPU periods were throttled in a 10-second sample after the fix (1 % before). I left the overcommit setting alone because it only affects new launches and the queue is empty.
- **Memory:** 27.2 GB actually used. The cgroup shows 137.2 of 137.4 GB only because of reclaimable page cache. No out-of-memory kills.
- **GPUs:** mine are 1–4. GPUs 5 and 6 are idle because nothing is queued.

**Health:**
- pilotCS_p062's flexion window ended in ERROR at 15:26, at t=3.824 (14 negative jacobians, failed to converge). That is a science result, so I did not restart it. The run moved on to its extension window as designed.
- All tmux services are up, so `ops/resume_all.sh` was not needed.

**Needs a person:**
- Decide the next FEBio batch after the pilots.
- Fix the scheduler (h06/h18) so a new run never takes cores inside a running run's core list, and so each run's cores stay inside one NUMA node.
- The split runs' flexion/extension windows still cannot restart after a scheduler restart or server stop.
- The QA checker (`biocage_qa`) is still not watched by the h23 watchdog.

I also added a note to my memory about this second occurrence of the core-sharing gap.

Files are in `work/agents/foreman/`:
- report_20261104_1527.md
- status.json

Two lines were appended to `work/ops/foreman_actions.log`.
